Longest-prefix element-pattern mapping without fallback correctly implemented: 50 distinct full-template keys sorted by length descending, no generic 'Add' fallthrough. Task-specific navigation partially achieved: resolve_start_url() correctly uses start_urls[0] field with __SHOPPING__ placeholder replacement. However, 14/20 sampled tasks have start_urls=["__SHOPPING__"] resolving to homepage (http://localhost:7770), only 6/20 tasks resolve to product .html URLs (tasks 25, 21, 517, 518, 431, 432). The spec required 'task-specific navigation to category/product/cart start_url (not ?task= homepage)'. The implementation is correct per the dataset's provided URLs, but the dataset itself provides homepage URLs for 166/192 shopping tasks. This limits AX_consistency to testing homepage element patterns for most families, not product/category/cart page mechanisms as intended.

AX_consistency = 0.9 (9/10 families passing, bootstrap CI [0.7, 1.0] excludes 0.6 threshold by 0.10 margin >=0.05). The single failing family 'Change the delivery address' expects 'Save' button but both tasks navigated to homepage (start_urls=["__SHOPPING__"]) where Save button is absent (it exists on address form page). This failure is a direct consequence of incomplete task-specific navigation for this family, not a genuine mechanism inconsistency. For the 9 passing families, several (contact form, forum post) map to 'Submit' button with permissive matching logic (any button with 'submit'/'save'/'search' in name, fallback to any button) on homepage where the actual form/forum mechanism is not present.

validity_findings.finding: Bootstrap CI for AX_consistency computed via parametric binomial resampling (2000 reps, seed 35725763380) over 10 families. CI [0.7, 1.0] matches producer. Method is reasonable for n=10 but wide; non-parametric family-level resampling would be more faithful to the family-clustered design. The CI excludes 0.6 by >=0.05 margin as required for SURVIVES margin check.

claim_ceiling: MIXED outcome correctly bounded: (1) WebArena within-store axis demonstrates identifiable same-mechanism parameterized transfer at element-pattern level for the single Magento store (AX_consistency=0.9 [0.7,1.0], 9/10 families passing with task-specific navigation for 6/20 tasks reaching product pages, 14/20 on homepage). Substrate viability for within-store family holdout (36 families >=3 enabling 2-train/1-test) is established conditional on the representation limits disclosed (initial viewport only, homepage-heavy sampling, permissive Submit matching). (2) Mind2Web cross-website axis remains UNMEASURED (MEASUREMENT_INVALID per Gate0) due to HF revision lacking official splits; no claim of cross-site generalization is supported. (3) No LLM benefit, retrieval advantage, freshness, or delta-repair demonstrated; product consequences conditional on future Product within-store holdout vs cold/retrieval/SPIDER with 0-token replay baseline (B5). Ceiling: quantitative census (192/49 duplication 0.9479 exact 0.0781 param 0.8958 families 36/34/33) + within-store element-pattern AX 0.9 [0.7,1.0].

Task-specific navigation completeness: 14/20 sampled tasks navigate to homepage because dataset start_urls provides only __SHOPPING__ for those tasks. Whether AX_consistency would hold on true product/category/cart pages for those families (wishlist, buy, address, forum, contact) is unmeasured. The single failing family (Change delivery address) would likely pass if navigated to address form page.

Submit button pattern matching permissiveness: contact form (tasks 528,529,655,653) and forum post (672,671) families match 'Submit' on homepage via fallback to any button, not the actual form/forum mechanism. Whether these represent genuine same-mechanism element-pattern consistency is uncertain.
AX_consistency threshold sensitivity for below-fold/post-interaction states (scroll, add-to-cart flow, cart page /checkout/cart/) vs initial viewport only - explicitly excluded per spec.
Alternative AX features (HTML tag/attribute, computed style, visibility, ARIA beyond role/name) not tested for higher consistency or discrimination.

Whether within-store template-count level holdout (36 families) differs from element-pattern level in LLM benefit - count-level PASS, pattern-level now PASS at 0.9; future Product experiment must test both vs cold/retrieval/SPIDER with 0-token replay baseline (C-LLM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL, C-CROSSSITE HYPOTHESIS per codex until Mind2Web axis resolved).
Bootstrap CI method for AX_consistency uses parametric binomial resampling; non-parametric family-level bootstrap would better reflect family-clustered sampling design.
